how: San Francisco Rec & Park runs a free first-come public archery range in Golden Gate Park at 47th Ave and Fulton St; bows can be rented at the nearby SF Archery Pro Shop, and Palomo Archery holds fortnightly Friday-night sessions.
Bay Area Competitive Cricket and San Ramon Tri-Valley Cricket host weekend practice and league games listed on Meetup, part of a large Bay Area amateur cricket scene.
Halberstadt Fencers' Club in the Mission runs an introduction to fencing course covering foil, epee and sabre with equipment provided, followed by beginner classes per weapon.
Yerba Buena Ice Skating & Bowling Center in Yerba Buena Gardens has a public ice rink open for recreational skating, with skate rental.
venue: Yerba Buena Ice Skating and Bowling Center

how: Touchstone's Mission Cliffs has top-rope and lead walls plus bouldering, with classes and private lessons; day passes are listed at $30-35.
San Francisco Judo Institute, a non-profit dojo on Taraval Street, and Soko Joshi Judo Club run judo classes for ages 8 to adults.
Korean Martial Arts Center on Ocean Ave teaches taekwondo to kids and adults, and SF Martial Arts Club at the African American Art & Culture Complex offers taekwondo alongside boxing and muay thai.
ABADA-Capoeira San Francisco in the Mission offers a free fundamentals class for new adults on the first Tuesday of each month, and ABADA-Capoeira Oakland holds drop-in classes.
Pickup ultimate groups such as South Bay and Peninsula Pickup Ultimate (Belmont) and social frisbee meetups in San Francisco run regular open games.
venue: South Bay and Peninsula Pickup Ultimate

how: East Bay Regional Parks run family tent sites, cabins, group and backpacking campsites bookable via ReserveAmerica, including at Anthony Chabot above Oakland.
venue: East Bay Regional Park District campgrounds

how: Bay Area Dragons (Foster City) offer free weekend dragon boat lessons, and Oakland Renegades train at the Alameda Grand Street ramp with the first three sessions free.
City Kayak at Pier 40, South Beach Harbor, runs seatouring kayak and surfski classes and rents kayaks for the bay and McCovey Cove.
City Kayak at Pier 40 teaches a Beginning SUP lesson and rents stand-up paddleboards.

The Dolphin Club and South End Rowing Club, both on Aquatic Park Cove, run member rowing programmes with an introductory orientation, and Open Water Rowing Center in Sausalito offers a beginner clinic.
San Francisco Bay Area Curling Club runs 90-minute learn-to-curl sessions at its dedicated Oakland facility (8450 Enterprise Way), no experience needed.
venue: San Francisco Bay Area Curling Club

how: City-run Oakland Stables on Skyline Blvd offers riding lessons and training, and Miwok Livery in Mill Valley runs trail rides in the Marin Headlands.
Fort Funston's coastal cliffs are a long-established hang gliding site, flown from the old Nike site above the beach.
Chabot Space & Science Center in the Oakland hills holds free public telescope viewings on Friday and Saturday evenings, weather permitting, using three historic telescopes.
San Francisco Community Music Center offers a Beginning Group Guitar for Adults class with no prerequisites, plus private lessons on guitar-family instruments.
San Francisco Community Music Center's Anything Goes Chorus I welcomes singers with little to no experience, and San Francisco Gay Men's Chorus runs auditions each season.
Circus Center in Cole Valley offers adult classes in aerial, acrobatics, flying trapeze, contortion, juggling and clown, including a beginners track.
San Francisco Ballet School runs adult classes from absolute beginner level, in person at 455 Franklin St and on Zoom.
La Bruja in Berkeley and Come Dance Marin run weekly tango classes and milongas, and San Francisco Bay Area Tango hosts a beginner-friendly milonga.
SF Sketchers organise regular outdoor sketching meetups such as Dock of the Bay Sketching around the Bay Area.
Sketchboard Co. runs weekly nude figure drawing sessions at Monument in San Francisco and Oakland Grove, and Abrams Claghorn Gallery in Albany holds Figure Drawing Fridays.
Art School of SF Bay in San Rafael runs a 16-session Oil and Acrylic Painting course.
Arts & Crafts for Team on Ritch St runs a 45-minute Botanical Soy Candle Making workshop for beginners.
Public Glass in Bayview offers beginner hot-glass workshops such as Play With Fire (3 hours, no experience needed).
Public Glass in Bayview lists an intro flameworking class alongside its hot-glass workshops.
Richmond Art Center runs eight-week beginning and intermediate wheel courses.
Richmond Art Center runs Evening and Afternoon Hand & Wheel courses combining handbuilding and throwing.
Modern Sailing School & Club in Sausalito and Berkeley teaches ASA 101 and later courses on 30-32 ft keelboats over two weekends or four weekdays.
Tradewinds Sailing runs a three-day ASA 101 Basic Keelboat course on Catalina Capri 22s on San Francisco Bay, with three students per instructor.
San Francisco SCUBA Schools offers PADI Open Water courses with pool sessions in Pacifica, and Pinnacles Dive Center in Marin certifies in San Francisco and Monterey.

San Francisco Conservatory of Music's Adult Extension Division runs a 13-week Class Piano I & II, and Blue Bear School of Music offers adult group classes and private lessons at Fort Mason and Mission Bay.
venue: San Francisco Conservatory of Music Adult Extension

how: San Francisco Comedy College on Post St teaches improv, sketch and stand-up classes, and The Improv's Bayfront Theater has listed improv courses.
San Francisco Comedy College on Post St teaches stand-up courses, and a veteran who performs at the Punch Line and Cobb's taught a four-week stand-up class in Oakland.
Ocean Beach is one of the Bay Area's top surf spots with several surf shops, and guided beginner lessons with boards and wetsuits run from near Judah St.
Indian Rock Park in Berkeley has long been a practice site for rock climbing and bouldering, used by Sierra Club climbers since the 1930s.
Mount Tamalpais in Marin has over 100 miles of trails and fire roads with bay and ocean views, and the Presidio has more than 24 miles of hiking trails.
Mount Tamalpais fire roads and trails are widely used for running, and the Dipsea Race from Mill Valley to Stinson Beach is the oldest cross-country trail race in the US.
Bay Pickleball hosts PickleFun sessions in San Francisco, and Marin Pickleball for All runs open play at indoor and outdoor courts.
Requires a dedicated ice track; none exists in the Bay Area, and the nearest US tracks are at Park City, Utah and Lake Placid, New York.
Requires snow-covered jumping hills; none exist in the Bay Area, and the nearest facilities are around Lake Tahoe or farther east.
No snow at sea level in the Bay Area; resorts in the Lake Tahoe area in the Sierra Nevada are roughly 3.5 to 4 hours' drive away.
The Bay Area has no snow season; the nearest snowfall is in the Sierra Nevada around Lake Tahoe, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours' drive away.
The Bay Area has no big walls; the nearest are in Yosemite Valley (El Capitan), roughly 4 hours' drive away.
No camel racing tradition or tracks exist in the Bay Area; the sport is centred in the Gulf states, Australia and Central Asia.
Requires working elephants, which are not kept for recreation in the Bay Area; the sport is played in Nepal, Thailand and India.
Mangroves do not grow naturally this far north on the California coast; bay and salt-marsh sea kayaking is available instead.

Golden City Dance Collective on Mission St runs progressive bachata and salsa classes on Mondays with no partner or experience needed, and Dance Fridays at Space 550 offers beginner bachata and salsa lessons before its social.
Lindy in the Park holds a free beginner swing lesson on Sundays behind the de Young Museum in Golden Gate Park, and The 9:20 Special on Sutter St is the Bay Area's largest Lindy Hop venue.
venue: Lindy in the Park (Golden Gate Park)

how: Theatre Flamenco of San Francisco, founded 1966, runs weekly flamenco classes for all levels at 670 S. Van Ness Ave, and Studio Danza on Mission St also offers flamenco classes.
Murphy Irish Dancers teach beginners from age 4 to adults in San Francisco and on the Peninsula, and the Irish Center SF lists several schools including Healy and Kennelly.
Songbird Dance Studio on Fern St offers a Pole Foundation Level 1 class, and Empress Ouroboros on Laguna St runs beginner pole choreography.
Ali Akbar College of Music in San Rafael teaches tabla in the North Indian classical tradition in person and online, with group sessions each term.
Chitresh Das Institute teaches Kathak at all levels including beginners, with Fall 2026 classes in Cupertino, San Mateo and San Ramon and its office in San Francisco.
Bay Area Video Coalition offers short courses on cinematography, DaVinci Resolve colour correction and audio post-production through learn.bavc.org.
Knit One Crochet, Too, Richmond Knit & Crochet (San Francisco) and East Bay Knitting Community run regular open knit and crochet meetups.
Metalworks SF in North Beach teaches jewelry making to beginners and experienced makers, and Richmond Art Center runs a six-session Introduction to Silversmithing course.

Low Light Darkroom, a volunteer-run nonprofit lab in Union Square, offers studio time for developing film and printing, and Sixth Street Photography Workshop runs a weekly darkroom workshop at SOMArts.
Garnish Music Production in San Francisco and Blue Bear School of Music offer music production and DJ courses, with CourseHorse listing further classes.
Blue Bear School of Music runs group and private DJ classes taught by local DJs, and DJ4LIFE Academy in SoMa offers three levels of DJ instruction.

San Francisco Fog RFC, an inclusive club in the Northern California Rugby Football Union, runs a free beginner crash course on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and San Francisco Golden Gate RFC fields several teams.
venue: San Francisco Fog Rugby Football Club

how: Oakland Ice Center (Sharks Ice) runs adult beginner and intermediate hockey classes feeding into the Sharks Ice Adult Hockey League, plus drop-in pickup and stick time.
San Francisco Taiko Dojo, the oldest taiko school in the US, runs beginning adult and child taiko classes with registration through its website.

CourseHorse lists San Francisco tap classes at all levels, the San Francisco Tap Festival at Dance Mission Theater welcomes adult beginners, and the City of South San Francisco runs an adult tap course.
venue: San Francisco Tap Festival (Dance Mission Theater)

how: ClassBento lists San Francisco screen printing classes at around $110 per session, and RayKo's print studio has hosted screen printing teaching.

San Francisco Center for the Book at 375 Rhode Island St teaches bookbinding and letterpress, including a three-hour Introduction to Bookbinding, and Graphic Arts Workshop has run two-day hardcover bookbinding workshops.
venue: San Francisco Center for the Book

how: Maker Studio on Octavia St runs a beginner three-hour stained glass workshop, and Cradle of the Sun Stained Glass is a long-running studio teaching cutting, foiling and soldering.
Richmond Art Center runs a belt-making class (cut, tool, stain and bevel heavy leather), and Timmy May's in Alameda offers leather workshops such as a valet tray.
Potrero del Sol skatepark (about 16,000 sq ft with a bowl, snake run and street section) and SoMa West Skate Plaza are free public skateparks, and San Francisco Skate Club teaches kids.
Art School of SF Bay in San Rafael runs a 10-session Watercolor 101, and Richmond Art Center offers beginning and intermediate watercolor courses.
Digital Photo Academy runs camera-controls classes and in-the-field photo workshops at the Ferry Building, Chinatown, the Embarcadero and Golden Gate Park.
